newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisian president urges tighter budget in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Tunisian president urges tighter budget in 1998.

text.p: The President on Tuesday instructed the Finance Minister to curb expenses in the 1998 budget now being prepared, official sources said.
President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali "insisted on the necessity of continuing efforts to curb expenses to reach internal and external financial balances," the sources said.
Ben Ali also recommended to Finance Minister Mohamed Jeri that studies of new projects must be completed before being put into the budget.
The budget must be set up to establish the national priorities of the 9th development plan 1997-2001 and modernisation of the economy, he also instructed him.
The budget for the fiscal year which started on January 1 was 8.01 billion dinars, 10.8 percent up on 1996.

The government hopes to keep the 1997 net budget deficit at 640 million dinars or three per cent of gross domestic product. The 1996 deficit was 575 million dinars and three percent of GDP. ($=1.08 dinar)
